functions: Journal lines for an AASB 16 lease from its liability and right-of-use schedules

/*  FUNCTION NAME:  LeaseJournalλ
    DESCRIPTION:*//**Journal lines for an AASB 16 lease: initial recognition, interest, payments and depreciation, from the lease and right-of-use schedules*/

LeaseJournalλ = LAMBDA(
//  Parameter Declaration
    [LeaseSchedule],
    [ROUSchedule],
    [Accounts],
    LET(
    //  Help
        Help,           TRIM(TEXTSPLIT(
                            "FUNCTION:      →LeaseJournalλ(LeaseSchedule, ROUSchedule, [Accounts])¶" &
                            "DESCRIPTION:   →Journal lines for an AASB 16 lease from its liability and right-of-use schedules.¶NOTES!         →Returns a header row and two lines for each entry: period, account,¶               →debit, credit and narration. Period 0 recognises the right-of-use asset¶               →and the lease liability (AASB 16 paragraphs 22, 23 and 26), and takes the¶               →rest of the asset's cost, the payments at or before commencement less¶               →incentives received and the initial direct costs of paragraph 24(b) and¶               →(c), to the cash account. A restoration estimate in the cost, paragraph¶               →24(d), is a provision under AASB 137 (paragraph 25), not cash: journal it¶               →from cash to the provision yourself. Each later period¶               →adds the interest that unwinds the liability (paragraphs 36(a), 37 and¶               →38(a)), the payment that reduces it (paragraph 36(b)) and the asset's¶               →depreciation (paragraphs 31 and 32), from the columns of LeaseScheduleλ()¶               →and ROUScheduleλ(). A nil amount gives no line; a negative one swaps its¶               →debit and credit. Amounts are as the schedules give them, unrounded, and¶               →debits equal credits in every period. Present the interest apart from the¶               →depreciation (paragraph 49). Arithmetic only: it does not decide the lease¶               →term, the payments or the rate. AASB 16 compilation read 18 November 2026.¶" &
                            "WEBPAGE:       →https://github.com/ryanduguid/Ozzit/blob/main/docs/australian-modelling.md¶" &
                            "VERSION:       →18 Nov 2026¶" &
                            "PARAMETERS:    →¶" &
                            "LeaseSchedule  →(Required) The four rows LeaseScheduleλ() returns for the lease.¶" &
                            "ROUSchedule    →(Required) The three rows ROUScheduleλ() returns for its right-of-use asset.¶" &
                            "Accounts       →(Optional: Default = Right-of-use asset, Lease liability, Interest expense, Cash, Depreciation expense,¶" &
                            "               →Accumulated depreciation) Up to six account names or codes, in that order. A blank keeps its default.¶" &
                            "EXAMPLES:      →¶" &
                            "→Formula (oz is assumed to be the module's name)¶" &
                            "→=oz.LeaseJournalλ(oz.LeaseScheduleλ({105}, 0.05), oz.ROUScheduleλ(100, 1))¶" &
                            "→Result¶" &
                            "→Period, Account, Debit, Credit, Narration¶" &
                            "→0, Right-of-use asset, 100, , Lease liability recognised at commencement¶" &
                            "→0, Lease liability, , 100, Lease liability recognised at commencement¶" &
                            "→1, Interest expense, 5, , Interest on the lease liability¶" &
                            "→1, Lease liability, , 5, Interest on the lease liability¶" &
                            "→1, Lease liability, 105, , Lease payment¶" &
                            "→1, Cash, , 105, Lease payment¶" &
                            "→1, Depreciation expense, 100, , Depreciation of the right-of-use asset¶" &
                            "→1, Accumulated depreciation, , 100, Depreciation of the right-of-use asset",
                            "→", "¶"
                        )),
    //  Check inputs - Omitted required arguments
        Help?,          OR( ISOMITTED( LeaseSchedule), ISOMITTED( ROUSchedule)),
    //  A blank account cell, or one left off the end, keeps its default
        Defaults,       {"Right-of-use asset", "Lease liability", "Interest expense", "Cash", "Depreciation expense", "Accumulated depreciation"},
        Given,          IF( ISOMITTED( Accounts), "", IF( TRIM( Accounts & "") = "", "", Accounts)),
        Listed,         TOROW( Given),
        Names,          IF( EXPAND( Listed, 1, 6, "") = "", Defaults, EXPAND( Listed, 1, 6, "")),
        ValidNames?,    COLUMNS( Listed) <= 6,
        ValidSchedules?, IFERROR( AND( ROWS( LeaseSchedule) = 4, ROWS( ROUSchedule) = 3,
                            ISNUMBER( LeaseSchedule), ISNUMBER( ROUSchedule)), FALSE),
        ScheduleMessage, "LeaseJournalλ needs the four rows of LeaseScheduleλ() and the three rows of ROUScheduleλ(), all numbers.",
        NamesMessage,   "LeaseJournalλ takes at most six account names.",
    //  Each period has three entries, interest, payment and depreciation, so entry i
    //  belongs to period INT((i - 1) / 3) + 1. A schedule shorter than the other, as the
    //  liability is for payments in advance, has nil entries in its missing periods.
        Spans,          MAX( COLUMNS( LeaseSchedule), COLUMNS( ROUSchedule)),
        Along,          LAMBDA( Block, Which, TOCOL( EXPAND( CHOOSEROWS( Block, Which), 1, Spans, 0))),
        Entry,          SEQUENCE( 3 * Spans),
        Period,         INT( ( Entry - 1) / 3) + 1,
        Kind,           MOD( Entry - 1, 3) + 1,
        Amount,         CHOOSE( Kind, INDEX( Along( LeaseSchedule, 3), Period), INDEX( Along( LeaseSchedule, 2), Period),
                            INDEX( Along( ROUSchedule, 2), Period)),
        Debit,          CHOOSE( Kind, INDEX( Names, 3), INDEX( Names, 2), INDEX( Names, 5)),
        Credit,         CHOOSE( Kind, INDEX( Names, 2), INDEX( Names, 4), INDEX( Names, 6)),
        Narration,      CHOOSE( Kind, "Interest on the lease liability", "Lease payment", "Depreciation of the right-of-use asset"),
    //  At commencement the asset takes the liability and, from cash, the rest of its cost
        Recognised,     INDEX( LeaseSchedule, 1, 1),
        Entries,        VSTACK(
                            HSTACK( 0, INDEX( Names, 1), INDEX( Names, 2), Recognised, "Lease liability recognised at commencement"),
                            HSTACK( 0, INDEX( Names, 1), INDEX( Names, 4), INDEX( ROUSchedule, 1, 1) - Recognised,
                                "Rest of the right-of-use asset's cost at commencement"),
                            HSTACK( Period, Debit, Credit, Amount, Narration)),
    //  Two lines an entry, debit then credit; a negative amount swaps the accounts
        Kept,           FILTER( Entries, CHOOSECOLS( Entries, 4) <> 0, ""),
        Empty?,         ROWS( Kept) * COLUMNS( Kept) = 1,
        Line,           SEQUENCE( 2 * ROWS( Kept)),
        Pick,           INT( ( Line - 1) / 2) + 1,
        Credit?,        MOD( Line - 1, 2) = 1,
        Value,          INDEX( Kept, Pick, 4),
        Lines,          HSTACK( INDEX( Kept, Pick, 1),
                            INDEX( Kept, Pick, IF( ( Value < 0) = Credit?, 2, 3)),
                            IF( Credit?, "", ABS( Value)),
                            IF( Credit?, ABS( Value), ""),
                            INDEX( Kept, Pick, 5)),
        Header,         {"Period", "Account", "Debit", "Credit", "Narration"},
        Result,         IF( Empty?, Header, VSTACK( Header, Lines)),
    //  Return Result, Help, or the message
        Return,         IF( Help?, 2, IF( NOT( ValidSchedules?), 3, IF( NOT( ValidNames?), 4, 1))),
        CHOOSE( Return, Result, Help, ScheduleMessage, NamesMessage)
    )
);
Hire purchase or chattel mortgage schedule in cents, the last payment taking the rounding

/*  FUNCTION NAME:  HPScheduleλ
    DESCRIPTION:*//**Hire purchase or chattel mortgage schedule in cents: opening, payment, interest, principal and closing for each period*/

HPScheduleλ = LAMBDA(
//  Parameter Declaration
    [Financed],
    [AnnualRate],
    [Periods],
    [PeriodsPerYear],
    [InAdvance],
    [Balloon],
    LET(
    //  Help
        Help,           TRIM(TEXTSPLIT(
                            "FUNCTION:      →HPScheduleλ(Financed, AnnualRate, Periods, [PeriodsPerYear], [InAdvance], [Balloon])¶" &
                            "DESCRIPTION:   →Schedule of a hire purchase or chattel mortgage, in cents.¶NOTES!         →Returns five rows, one column a payment: opening balance, payment,¶               →interest, principal and closing balance. The rate per period is¶               →PeriodRateλ(AnnualRate, PeriodsPerYear). The level payment is¶               →LevelPaymentλ() at that rate, divided by 1 + rate for payments in¶               →advance, rounded to the cent. Interest is rounded to the cent each period,¶               →charged on the balance after the payment when payments are in advance.¶               →The final payment takes the rounding difference, so the last closing¶               →balance is the Balloon exactly; the Balloon is paid at the end of the last¶               →period. In advance the last period's interest is the Balloon's share¶               →Rate / (1 + Rate), in cents, which can be a cent off interest on the¶               →balance left after the last payment. Financed and Balloon are in whole¶               →cents. For the rate a contract's instalment implies, pass¶               →AnnualRateλ(RATE(Periods, -Instalment, Financed, -Balloon, InAdvance), PeriodsPerYear).¶               →For a nominal rate that compounds with each payment, pass EFFECT(Nominal,¶               →PeriodsPerYear). Bookkeeping arithmetic only: it does not work out the tax¶               →treatment, such as Division 240 of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997 for¶               →a hire purchase, or GST input tax credits, and leaves out fees.¶" &
                            "WEBPAGE:       →https://github.com/ryanduguid/Ozzit/blob/main/docs/australian-modelling.md¶" &
                            "VERSION:       →20 Nov 2026¶" &
                            "PARAMETERS:    →¶" &
                            "Financed       →(Required) Amount financed at the start, in whole cents: the price less any deposit or trade-in.¶" &
                            "AnnualRate     →(Required) Effective annual interest rate.¶" &
                            "Periods        →(Required) Number of payments, a whole number of at least 1.¶" &
                            "PeriodsPerYear →(Optional: Default = 12) Payments a year: 52 weekly, 26 fortnightly, 12 monthly, 4 quarterly.¶" &
                            "InAdvance      →(Optional: Default = FALSE) TRUE or 1 when each payment falls at the start of its period.¶" &
                            "Balloon        →(Optional: Default = 0) Balloon or residual still owed after the last payment, in whole cents.¶" &
                            "EXAMPLES:      →¶" &
                            "→Formula (oz is assumed to be the module's name)¶" &
                            "→=oz.HPScheduleλ(1000, 0.1, 3, 1)¶" &
                            "→Result¶" &
                            "→1000.00, 697.89, 365.57¶" &
                            "→ 402.11, 402.11, 402.13¶" &
                            "→ 100.00,  69.79,  36.56¶" &
                            "→ 302.11, 332.32, 365.57¶" &
                            "→ 697.89, 365.57,   0.00",
                            "→", "¶"
                        )),
    //  Check inputs - Omitted required arguments
        Help?,          OR( ISOMITTED( Financed), ISOMITTED( AnnualRate), ISOMITTED( Periods)),
    //  A blank optional cell is not an omitted argument, so test for both
        PerYear,        IF( ISOMITTED( PeriodsPerYear), 12, IF( TRIM( PeriodsPerYear & "") = "", 12, PeriodsPerYear)),
        Advance?,       IF( ISOMITTED( InAdvance), FALSE, IF( TRIM( InAdvance & "") = "", FALSE, InAdvance)),
        Final,          IF( ISOMITTED( Balloon), 0, IF( TRIM( Balloon & "") = "", 0, Balloon)),
    //  One agreement: single numbers, TRUE, FALSE, 1 or 0 for InAdvance, and terms that
    //  make a schedule. Arithmetic would read "1000" as 1000, so text is refused. The
    //  amounts are whole cents. Allow binary rounding when reading the amount and
    //  scaling to cents (for example 10.1 * 3), within the thousandth-of-a-cent cap.
        Single?,        LAMBDA( x, AND( ROWS( x) = 1, COLUMNS( x) = 1, ISNUMBER( x))),
        Cents?,         LAMBDA( x, LET( Scaled, x * 100,
                                        Difference, ABS( Scaled - ROUND( Scaled, 0)),
                                        AND( Difference < 0.001, Difference <= MAX( 1, ABS( Scaled)) * 2^-51))),
        Valid?,         IFERROR( AND( Single?( Financed), Single?( AnnualRate), Single?( Periods), Single?( PerYear),
                            Single?( Final), OR( --Advance? = 0, --Advance? = 1), Financed > 0, AnnualRate > -1,
                            Periods >= 1, Periods = INT( Periods), PerYear > 0, Final >= 0, Cents?( Financed),
                            Cents?( Final)), FALSE),
        TermsMessage,   "HPScheduleλ needs single numbers: Financed above 0 and a Balloon from 0 in whole cents, AnnualRate above -1, a whole number of Periods from 1 and PeriodsPerYear above 0, and TRUE, FALSE, 1 or 0 for InAdvance.",
        Count,          IF( Valid?, Periods, 1),
        Rate,           IF( Valid?, PeriodRateλ( AnnualRate, PerYear), 0),
        Principal,      IF( Valid?, ROUND( Financed, 2), 0),
        Owed,           IF( Valid?, ROUND( Final, 2), 0),
        Timing,         IF( Valid?, --Advance? <> 0, FALSE),
    //  The level payment in arrears, brought forward a period when paid in advance.
    //  LevelPaymentλ() returns a one-cell array; INDEX takes the number from it, because
    //  an array index would make CHOOSE pad the result to the size of the help.
        Payment,        ROUND( INDEX( LevelPaymentλ( Principal, SEQUENCE( 1, Count, Rate, 0), Owed), 1, 1) / IF( Timing, 1 + Rate, 1), 2),
        BalloonMessage, "HPScheduleλ needs a Balloon the payments can reach: no more than Financed grown at the rate.",
    //  Interest runs on the balance left after a payment in advance, or on the opening
    //  balance in arrears. The last closing balance is the Balloon by definition.
        Closings,       SCAN( Principal, SEQUENCE( 1, Count), LAMBDA( Balance, Each,
                            IF( Each = Count, Owed,
                                ROUND( Balance + ROUND( ( Balance - Timing * Payment) * Rate, 2) - Payment, 2)))),
        Openings,       IF( Count = 1, Principal, HSTACK( Principal, DROP( Closings, , -1))),
    //  In advance the last period's balance after its payment must grow to the Balloon,
    //  so its interest is the Balloon's share Rate / (1 + Rate), in cents.
        Last?,          SEQUENCE( 1, Count) = Count,
        Interest,       IF( Last? * Timing, ROUND( Owed * Rate / ( 1 + Rate), 2),
                            ROUND( ( Openings - Timing * Payment) * Rate, 2)),
        Payments,       IF( Last?, ROUND( Openings + Interest - Owed, 2), Payment),
        Result,         VSTACK( Openings, Payments, Interest, Payments - Interest, Closings),
    //  The largest Balloon is Financed grown at the rate with nil payments. Comparing
    //  whole cents refuses a cent beyond it, which a rounded payment of nil would hide.
        Reachable?,     Owed <= ROUND( Principal * ( 1 + Rate) ^ Count, 2),
    //  Return Result, Help, or the message
        Return,         IF( Help?, 2, IF( NOT( Valid?), 3, IF( NOT( Reachable?), 4, 1))),
        CHOOSE( Return, Result, Help, TermsMessage, BalloonMessage)
    )
);
Journal lines for a hire purchase or chattel mortgage from its schedule

/*  FUNCTION NAME:  HPJournalλ
    DESCRIPTION:*//**Journal lines for a hire purchase or chattel mortgage from its HPScheduleλ schedule: amount financed, interest, instalments and balloon*/

HPJournalλ = LAMBDA(
//  Parameter Declaration
    [HPSchedule],
    [Accounts],
    LET(
    //  Help
        Help,           TRIM(TEXTSPLIT(
                            "FUNCTION:      →HPJournalλ(HPSchedule, [Accounts])¶" &
                            "DESCRIPTION:   →Journal lines for a hire purchase or chattel mortgage from its schedule.¶NOTES!         →Returns a header row and two lines for each entry: period, account,¶               →debit, credit and narration. Period 0 debits the asset and credits the¶               →liability with the amount financed. Each later period charges the¶               →interest to the liability and pays the instalment from cash, from the¶               →columns of HPScheduleλ(), and the last period pays the Balloon. A nil¶               →amount gives no line; a negative one swaps its debit and credit. Debits¶               →equal credits in every period, and the liability closes at nil. Rename the¶               →liability for a chattel mortgage. Bookkeeping only: it does not journal a¶               →deposit, a trade-in, fees, GST input tax credits, depreciation or the tax¶               →treatment, such as Division 240 of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997.¶" &
                            "WEBPAGE:       →https://github.com/ryanduguid/Ozzit/blob/main/docs/australian-modelling.md¶" &
                            "VERSION:       →18 Nov 2026¶" &
                            "PARAMETERS:    →¶" &
                            "HPSchedule     →(Required) The five rows HPScheduleλ() returns for the agreement.¶" &
                            "Accounts       →(Optional: Default = Asset at cost, Hire purchase liability, Interest expense, Cash) Up to four¶" &
                            "               →account names or codes, in that order. A blank keeps its default.¶" &
                            "EXAMPLES:      →¶" &
                            "→Formula (oz is assumed to be the module's name)¶" &
                            "→=oz.HPJournalλ(oz.HPScheduleλ(1000, 0.1, 1, 1, , 500))¶" &
                            "→Result¶" &
                            "→Period, Account, Debit, Credit, Narration¶" &
                            "→0, Asset at cost, 1000, , Amount financed¶" &
                            "→0, Hire purchase liability, , 1000, Amount financed¶" &
                            "→1, Interest expense, 100, , Interest on the agreement¶" &
                            "→1, Hire purchase liability, , 100, Interest on the agreement¶" &
                            "→1, Hire purchase liability, 600, , Instalment¶" &
                            "→1, Cash, , 600, Instalment¶" &
                            "→1, Hire purchase liability, 500, , Balloon¶" &
                            "→1, Cash, , 500, Balloon",
                            "→", "¶"
                        )),
    //  Check inputs - Omitted required arguments
        Help?,          ISOMITTED( HPSchedule),
    //  A blank account cell, or one left off the end, keeps its default
        Defaults,       {"Asset at cost", "Hire purchase liability", "Interest expense", "Cash"},
        Given,          IF( ISOMITTED( Accounts), "", IF( TRIM( Accounts & "") = "", "", Accounts)),
        Listed,         TOROW( Given),
        Names,          IF( EXPAND( Listed, 1, 4, "") = "", Defaults, EXPAND( Listed, 1, 4, "")),
        ValidNames?,    COLUMNS( Listed) <= 4,
        ValidSchedule?, IFERROR( AND( ROWS( HPSchedule) = 5, ISNUMBER( HPSchedule)), FALSE),
        ScheduleMessage, "HPJournalλ needs the five rows of HPScheduleλ(), all numbers.",
        NamesMessage,   "HPJournalλ takes at most four account names.",
    //  Each period has two entries, interest then the instalment, so entry i belongs to
    //  period INT((i - 1) / 2) + 1
        Spans,          COLUMNS( HPSchedule),
        Entry,          SEQUENCE( 2 * Spans),
        Period,         INT( ( Entry - 1) / 2) + 1,
        Interest?,      MOD( Entry - 1, 2) = 0,
        Amount,         INDEX( HPSchedule, IF( Interest?, 3, 2), Period),
        Debit,          IF( Interest?, INDEX( Names, 3), INDEX( Names, 2)),
        Credit,         IF( Interest?, INDEX( Names, 2), INDEX( Names, 4)),
        Narration,      IF( Interest?, "Interest on the agreement", "Instalment"),
        Entries,        VSTACK(
                            HSTACK( 0, INDEX( Names, 1), INDEX( Names, 2), INDEX( HPSchedule, 1, 1), "Amount financed"),
                            HSTACK( Period, Debit, Credit, Amount, Narration),
                            HSTACK( Spans, INDEX( Names, 2), INDEX( Names, 4), INDEX( HPSchedule, 5, Spans), "Balloon")),
    //  Two lines an entry, debit then credit; a negative amount swaps the accounts
        Kept,           FILTER( Entries, CHOOSECOLS( Entries, 4) <> 0, ""),
        Empty?,         ROWS( Kept) * COLUMNS( Kept) = 1,
        Line,           SEQUENCE( 2 * ROWS( Kept)),
        Pick,           INT( ( Line - 1) / 2) + 1,
        Credit?,        MOD( Line - 1, 2) = 1,
        Value,          INDEX( Kept, Pick, 4),
        Lines,          HSTACK( INDEX( Kept, Pick, 1),
                            INDEX( Kept, Pick, IF( ( Value < 0) = Credit?, 2, 3)),
                            IF( Credit?, "", ABS( Value)),
                            IF( Credit?, ABS( Value), ""),
                            INDEX( Kept, Pick, 5)),
        Header,         {"Period", "Account", "Debit", "Credit", "Narration"},
        Result,         IF( Empty?, Header, VSTACK( Header, Lines)),
    //  Return Result, Help, or the message
        Return,         IF( Help?, 2, IF( NOT( ValidSchedule?), 3, IF( NOT( ValidNames?), 4, 1))),
        CHOOSE( Return, Result, Help, ScheduleMessage, NamesMessage)
    )
);
Present value of each option's cash flows, such as a lease, hire purchase or loan, pre-tax

/*  FUNCTION NAME:  FinanceCompareλ
    DESCRIPTION:*//**Present value of each option's cash flows, such as a lease, hire purchase, loan or cash purchase, at one discount rate, pre-tax*/

FinanceCompareλ = LAMBDA(
//  Parameter Declaration
    [CashFlows],
    [DiscountRate],
    [PeriodsPerYear],
    [Labels],
    LET(
    //  Help
        Help,           TRIM(TEXTSPLIT(
                            "FUNCTION:      →FinanceCompareλ(CashFlows, DiscountRate, [PeriodsPerYear], [Labels])¶" &
                            "DESCRIPTION:   →Present value of each option's cash flows at one discount rate, before tax.¶NOTES!         →Returns a header row and one row per option: its label, the undiscounted¶               →total of its cash flows and their present value, before tax. Column 1 of¶               →CashFlows falls at the start and column k + 1 at the end of period k, a¶               →period being a year divided by PeriodsPerYear. DiscountRate is an¶               →effective annual rate, converted with PeriodRateλ(). Enter payments¶               →positive and receipts, such as the sale of the asset at the end, negative.¶               →A lease row is its payments, from column 2 in arrears or column 1 in¶               →advance. A hire purchase or loan row in arrears is 0, or the deposit, then¶               →the payment row of HPScheduleλ() with the Balloon added to the last; in¶               →advance it is that payment row from column 1, the deposit added to the¶               →first, then the Balloon in the next column. A cash purchase is the price in¶               →column 1. Pre-tax only: it leaves¶               →out income tax deductions, depreciation, GST input tax credits and Division¶               →240 of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997, which an after-tax comparison¶               →needs. It ranks nothing and recommends nothing.¶" &
                            "WEBPAGE:       →https://github.com/ryanduguid/Ozzit/blob/main/docs/australian-modelling.md¶" &
                            "VERSION:       →18 Nov 2026¶" &
                            "PARAMETERS:    →¶" &
                            "CashFlows      →(Required) One row per option, with a column for the start and one for the end of each period. A blank is nil.¶" &
                            "DiscountRate   →(Required) Effective annual discount rate.¶" &
                            "PeriodsPerYear →(Optional: Default = 12) Periods a year: 52 weekly, 26 fortnightly, 12 monthly, 4 quarterly, 1 yearly.¶" &
                            "Labels         →(Optional: Default = Option 1, Option 2 and so on) One label per option.¶" &
                            "EXAMPLES:      →¶" &
                            "→Formula (oz is assumed to be the module's name)¶" &
                            "→=oz.FinanceCompareλ({1000,0,0,0;0,350,350,350}, 0.05, 1, {""Cash"";""Lease""})¶" &
                            "→Result¶" &
                            "→Option, Undiscounted total, Present value (pre-tax)¶" &
                            "→Cash, 1000, 1000.00¶" &
                            "→Lease, 1050, 953.14",
                            "→", "¶"
                        )),
    //  Check inputs - Omitted required arguments
        Help?,          OR( ISOMITTED( CashFlows), ISOMITTED( DiscountRate)),
    //  A blank optional cell is not an omitted argument, so test for both
        PerYear,        IF( ISOMITTED( PeriodsPerYear), 12, IF( TRIM( PeriodsPerYear & "") = "", 12, PeriodsPerYear)),
    //  A blank flow is nil. SUM would leave text and TRUE out of a total, so they are
    //  refused rather than read as nil.
        Flows,          IF( TRIM( CashFlows & "") = "", 0, CashFlows),
        Options,        ROWS( Flows),
        ValidFlows?,    IFERROR( AND( ISNUMBER( Flows)), FALSE),
        ValidRate?,     IFERROR( AND( ROWS( DiscountRate) = 1, COLUMNS( DiscountRate) = 1, ISNUMBER( DiscountRate),
                            DiscountRate > -1, ROWS( PerYear) = 1, COLUMNS( PerYear) = 1, ISNUMBER( PerYear),
                            PerYear > 0), FALSE),
        Given,          IF( ISOMITTED( Labels), "", IF( TRIM( Labels & "") = "", "", Labels)),
        Listed,         TOCOL( Given),
        NoLabels?,      IF( ISOMITTED( Labels), TRUE, AND( ROWS( Labels) * COLUMNS( Labels) = 1, TRIM( Labels & "") = "")),
        ValidLabels?,   OR( NoLabels?, ROWS( Listed) = Options),
        Names,          IF( EXPAND( Listed, Options, 1, "") = "", "Option " & SEQUENCE( Options), EXPAND( Listed, Options, 1, "")),
        FlowsMessage,   "FinanceCompareλ needs every cash flow to be a number or blank.",
        RateMessage,    "FinanceCompareλ needs DiscountRate to be a single number above -1 and PeriodsPerYear a single number above 0.",
        LabelsMessage,  "FinanceCompareλ needs one label for each row of CashFlows.",
    //  Column k + 1 is discounted k periods at the rate per period
        Factors,        ( 1 + PeriodRateλ( DiscountRate, PerYear)) ^ -SEQUENCE( COLUMNS( Flows), 1, 0),
        Result,         VSTACK( {"Option", "Undiscounted total", "Present value (pre-tax)"},
                            HSTACK( Names, MMULT( Flows, SEQUENCE( COLUMNS( Flows), 1, 1, 0)), MMULT( Flows, Factors))),
    //  Return Result, Help, or the message
        Return,         IF( Help?, 2, IF( NOT( ValidFlows?), 3, IF( NOT( ValidRate?), 4, IF( NOT( ValidLabels?), 5, 1)))),
        CHOOSE( Return, Result, Help, FlowsMessage, RateMessage, LabelsMessage)
    )
);

Financial: "PAYGWithholdingλ   →Amount to withhold from a payment under the ATO's Schedule 1 formulas¶"
